title: Suppression of Inflammatory Responses Through GD3 Synthase (GD3S) Silencing Mediated by TLR4 Signaling: In Vitro and In Silico Analysis.
authors: Park, Jun-Young; Fukushi, Abekura; Kim, Hee-Do; Kuo, Han-His; Chang, Yu-Chan; Park, Daeui; Kim, Cheorl-Ho
one_liner_zh: 该文研究GD3合成酶沉默对炎症信号通路的抑制，并用分子对接和FMO计算分析GD3/GM3/LPS与TLR4-MD2复合物的结合，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作建模，但对象为糖脂-TLR4而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Glycosphingolipids (GSLs) regulate cell proliferation by modulating transmembrane signaling pathways. Gangliosides, as essential constituents of GSLs located on the cell membrane surface, contribute to diverse biological processes. Among them, ganglioside GD3 is found in neuronal precursors, TrkA receptor-expressing cells, and various neuronal populations, where it influences cell-cell interactions and metabolic activities. However, its immunity-related function and signaling mechanism remain unclear. In this study, we investigated THP-1-derived macrophages transfected with shGD3 synthesis (shGD3S) and observed reduced mRNA and protein expression of COX-2, iNOS, Myd88, TLR4, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Furthermore, activation of the MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways was diminished in shGD3S-transfected macrophages. We also examined the direct interaction between GD3 and TLR4, confirming that GD3 binds directly to TLR4. Using molecular docking simulations and fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations, we analyzed the binding affinities and hotspot residues of GD3, GM3, and LPS with the TLR4-MD2 complex. GD3 exhibited a higher binding affinity than GM3 and similar interaction energy to LPS, with Asp44 and Tyr82 identified as key hotspot residues. Ganglioside derivatives interacted with different TLR4 chains, with LPS and GM3 located near Arg90 and between fatty acid chains, while the linear carbohydrate moiety clustered around Phe121. These findings indicate that shGD3S-transfected macrophages suppress LPS-induced inflammatory responses by attenuating NF-kappaB, MAPK, and TLR4 signaling. Thus, sialyl-glycolipid GD3 appears to promote inflammatory responses in THP-1-derived macrophages.
abstract_zh: 鞘糖脂（GSLs）通过调节跨膜信号通路来调控细胞增殖。神经节苷脂作为位于细胞膜表面的GSLs的重要组成成分，参与多种生物过程。其中，神经节苷脂GD3存在于神经元前体细胞、表达TrkA受体的细胞以及多种神经元群体中，影响细胞间相互作用和代谢活动。然而，其免疫相关功能及信号机制尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们研究了转染shGD3合成（shGD3S）的THP-1来源巨噬细胞，观察到COX-2、iNOS、Myd88、TLR4及促炎细胞因子的mRNA和蛋白表达降低。此外，在shGD3S转染的巨噬细胞中，MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路的激活减弱。我们还检测了GD3与TLR4之间的直接相互作用，确认GD3直接结合TLR4。利用分子对接模拟和片段分子轨道（FMO）计算，我们分析了GD3、GM3和LPS与TLR4-MD2复合物的结合亲和力及热点残基。GD3表现出比GM3更高的结合亲和力，并与LPS具有相似的相互作用能，其中Asp44和Tyr82被鉴定为关键热点残基。神经节苷脂衍生物与不同的TLR4链相互作用，LPS和GM3位于Arg90附近及脂肪酸链之间，而线性碳水化合物部分聚集在Phe121周围。这些发现表明，shGD3S转染的巨噬细胞通过减弱NF-kappaB、MAPK和TLR4信号传导来抑制LPS诱导的炎症反应。因此，唾液酸糖脂GD3似乎在THP-1来源巨噬细胞中促进炎症反应。
